chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me of is from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris and Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad; and from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

If you are engaged in your wudu (ablution) and do not know whether you have washed your forearms or not, then repeat over them and over everything about which you doubted that you had not washed it or wiped it, from what Allah has named, so long as you remain in the state of wudu (ablution). But when you have risen from wudu (ablution), completed it, and entered another state, in salat (prayer) or otherwise, and then you doubt some part of what Allah has named among that for which Allah has made its wudu (ablution) obligatory upon you, then there is nothing upon you regarding it. If you doubt the wiping of your head and find moisture in your beard, then wipe with it over your head and over the upper side of your feet. But if you do not find moisture, then do not invalidate the wudu (ablution) by doubt, and continue in your salat (prayer). And if you become certain that you did not complete your wudu (ablution), then repeat from what you certainly left out until you complete the wudu (ablution).

Hammad said; Hariz said; Zurarah said: I said to him, A man left part of his forearm or part of his body out of the ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah. So he said: If he doubts and there is moisture on him while he is in his salat (prayer), he should wipe with it over it. But if he is certain, he should return and reapply over them, so long as he does not find moisture. If doubt enters him after he has entered his salat (prayer), then let him continue in his salat (prayer), and there is nothing upon him. But if he becomes certain, he should return and reapply water over it. And if he sees it while there is moisture on him, he should wipe over it and repeat the salat (prayer) out of certainty. And if he is doubtful, then there is nothing upon him in his doubt, so let him continue in his salat (prayer).

key_terms.اسْتَيْقَنَ: he became certain, indicating definite knowledge as opposed to doubt
key_terms.بَلَلًا: moisture, residual wetness relevant to completing wiping
key_terms.شَكَكْتَ: you doubted, meaning uncertainty regarding completion of a required act
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah, the obligatory full-body purification
key_terms.لِحْيَتِكَ: your beard, from which remaining moisture may be used for wiping
key_terms.مَسْحِ: wiping, the prescribed act of passing moisture over the head or feet in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.وُضُوئِكَ: your wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they doubt part of their wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) during or after completing it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling of doubt during and after wudu (ablution), and similarly addresses doubt in ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah. Doubt while still engaged in the act requires rectification, but doubt after completion and entry into another state such as salat (prayer) is disregarded unless one has certainty of omission.
